source_text: The diagram looks great now, but I do somewhat wonder about the role that the gray boxes play now.  If they aren't measureable in Lean, then to some extent maybe they don't "exist" in any reasonable way in our model — given that Lean is the model they *should* be modelled there otherwise they are basically just vibes.  Can you message codex-10 with findings?  I.e. do these features exist or not?

reply_text:
The message to codex-10 is sent and I'm parked on its reply; checking now that the job has actually started.㊥ ("message codex-10 with findings") Sent. The findings and your question went to codex-10 as a bell, and I'm parked on the reply. The short answer so far: on the records I read, only R9 has a Lean statement about what it is for; the other grey boxes are in Lean as names at most.

㊢ ("do these features exist or not?") Here is what I found and sent. Grey in the figure means no registry equation binds a Lean declaration at that node; it does not mean Lean never mentions the node.

| Node | In Lean | Running code (census of 2026-09-12, seven cells per node) |
|---|---|---|
| R9 No self-certification | A verdict model and a soundness proof over a finite recorded table; not a general proof | named only in one cell, absent in six |
| R10 Scheduled entrypoint | A run-record type and one open `sorry` (`wmRunsOnce`) | exists in two cells |
| R12 Two-layer calibration | A route-node name and route data only | exists in two cells |
| R20 Interoceptive tripwires | A route-node name, route data and a wiring test; no tripwire law | exists in two cells |
| R11 Hierarchical shared budget | A route-node name and wiring data only | absent in all seven |
| R15 Hierarchy and timescale | A route-node name and wiring data only | absent in all seven |
| CTAU-CLASS | Nothing; its registry row has no Lean target | the registry row points at code in `war_machine.clj` |

㊬ (what I checked today) Every Lean declaration in the table is still in `Holes.lean` at the line cited by the 2026-09-21 map (`MAP-rnode-to-lean-2026-09-21.md`), and `wmRunsOnce` is still `sorry`. The registry lists R9, R10, R11, R12, R15 and R20 as plumbing with no equation rows.

㊟ (limits of these findings) The Lean column rests on the three-week-old map plus my line check. I did not rerun its source searches or read Lean modules added since, and I did not recheck the code behind the runtime census. That is why I asked codex-10 for a verdict at current heads.

㊯ (what codex-10 was asked) For each of the seven nodes, one of three verdicts with the deciding declaration named: stated, named only, or absent. Also one line per node on whether running code implements it, and corrections to anything stale in the table above. It is read-only: no Lean, registry or figure changes, and any suggestion to drop a node or add a Lean statement comes back as a recommendation for you.

㊢ (status) The job is queued behind your own current turn with codex-10, so it starts when that turn ends.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("big white gaps") The boxes now sit in a tight grid, one column per stage. The grey boxes are at the foot of their own stage columns, so the separate band at the bottom is gone. Arrows run along the gaps between rows and columns and never pass behind a box.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("the text is unreadable at scale") The drawing is 1190 units wide where it was 1730, and the text is larger. Module names and term labels have moved off the drawing into the panel.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
("clicking into the gray nodes at the bottom does nothing of interest") Pointing at any box fills a panel under the grid, and clicking keeps that box selected.
- **Every box:** its name, stage, Lean modules, and the terms it uses and provides, coloured by how the Lean model carries each. The name comes from the paper's Pattern map table, or from the stage map where the table has no row.
- **Grey boxes:** the same, plus a line saying no Lean module is placed there. R10, for example, shows "Counts state change, not scheduler firing, as liveness."
- **Boxes with arrows:** their arrows stay lit and the others go pale.
- **R20:** its label on the frame is clickable too.
- **Legend and counts:** now inside the drawing; the old one had no key to the colours.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked) I served the site locally and drove Chromium at both window sizes above; there were no page errors.
- **Fit:** no label overflows its box, and nothing scrolls inside the frame.
- **Panel:** pointing at R10 and clicking R15 and R20 show their name and role; a click on the background clears it.
- **Selection:** clicking R4 lights its 12 arrows and pales the other 31, and holds while the pointer moves elsewhere.
- **Enlarging:** the box still opens on rest and closes from the margin.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what you may not like)
- **Box order:** within a column the script orders boxes to make arrows shortest, so R8 sits above R2 and R5 above R4.
- **Dense arrows:** the top three rows are still crowded between BELIEVE and EVALUATE; selecting a box is what makes them traceable.
- **Missing roles:** R3a, R19, the two CTAU boxes and SCAN have no row in the Pattern map, so they show a label and no role sentence.
- **SCAN's label:** "Scan observation model" is my wording, taken from the heading of `ScanLearning.lean`.
- **Phones:** at phone width the text is still too small to read.
